filename: Machine Learning for Online Sea Ice Bias Correction Within Global Ice‐Ocean Simulations.pdf
title: Machine Learning for Online Sea Ice Bias Correction Within Global Ice‐Ocean Simulations
parameterization_target: sea ice concentration increments / bias correction
code_availability: All data from the 1982–2017 DAZ21 experiment are available on Zenodo (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7818178). Code to implement the CNN into the SIS2 sea ice model and perform DA are available on Zenodo (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.10359842).
testbed_rationale: Publicly archived dataset of data assimilation increments and code implementing online ML correction inside a production global sea-ice model (SIS2 in GFDL SPEAR) provide a clear testbed for data-driven parameterization and bias correction.
pain_points: Online climate drift and large summertime residual errors requiring iterative online data augmentation to sample state trajectories post-correction
Model shock in online simulations characterized by 5-day cyclic shocks in sea ice extent because corrections are disproportionately applied to the thinnest ice category (5 cm)
Lack of mass, heat, and salt conservation when directly altering sea ice concentration state variables
Generalization challenges when moving from ocean-ice forced runs to fully coupled atmosphere-ocean-sea ice models with interactive feedbacks
extraction_notes: The paper uses CNNs trained to emulate data assimilation increments from an ensemble Kalman filter (EAKF) as an online subgrid bias-correction/parameterization within GFDL's SIS2/MOM6 models.
